crossRefs.note: A worthless person, a man of iniquity, is he who walks with a perverse mouth,
One winking with the eye causes sorrow, but a chattering fool will fall.
Make the heart of this people fat. Make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, hear with…
for this people’s heart has grown callous, their ears are dull of hearing, they have closed their eyes; or else perhaps…
For everyone who does evil hates the light, and doesn’t come to the light, lest his works would be exposed.
A worthless man devises mischief. His speech is like a scorching fire.
Their hands are on that which is evil to do it diligently. The ruler and judge ask for a bribe; and the powerful man…
Whereupon he promised with an oath to give her whatever she should ask.
She, being prompted by her mother, said, “Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptizer.”
But the governor said, “Why? What evil has he done?” But they cried out exceedingly, saying, “Let him be crucified!”

translations.web: One who winks his eyes to plot perversities, one who compresses his lips, is bent on evil.
translations.bsb: He who winks his eye devises perversity; he who purses his lips is bent on evil.
translations.kjv: He shutteth his eyes to devise froward things: moving his lips he bringeth evil to pass.
translations.asv: He that shutteth his eyes, it is to devise perverse things: He that compresseth his lips bringeth evil to pass.
